Two tools, one goal

Buying gear well means solving two different problems: figuring out what to get in the first place, and knowing whether something you're already eyeing is actually right for your trip. Gear Wrangler does both.

Finding gear to buy

For when you're starting from scratch

Every gear review site ranks products the same way: for the average person, on average terrain, with an average budget. But you're one specific person with one specific trip in mind, and the pad that's "best overall" might be the wrong pad for you.

someone who barely needs it someone who needs it a lot

That curve is sometimes called diminishing marginal utility: the same extra ounce of warmth is worth a lot to one person and almost nothing to another, depending on where they already sit on the curve. A thru-hiker who's already warm enough needs less weight, not more warmth. A weekend camper who's always cold needs the opposite. Neither is well served by a single "best" answer.

Checking gear you're considering

For when you already have something in mind

Sometimes you don't need a recommendation — you need a straight answer on something specific. Maybe you're eyeing a jacket a friend recommended, or something you already own, and want to know if it's actually right for your trip. This part of Gear Wrangler is built for that: trip conditions are set once, and you can check any item against them.

An expedition gets set up once

Coldest expected night, terrain, rain, budget guidance — entered by whoever's leading the trip.

Search it in our database, or type in the specs if it's something we don't carry.

Don't bring it, it's fine, or here's something better for about the same money — with the reason spelled out.

Where do these numbers come from?

We check store prices once a day where stores allow it, and show the date of the last check. Other new-item prices come from 2026 gear guides and retailer listings, and show the month they were last updated. "On sale" means the store lists a higher regular price. "Price drop" means the price fell from the highest we've seen in the last 90 days. Sale prices may only apply to some colors or sizes, so confirm the price on the store's page before you buy. Amazon picks link to a search, not one exact listing, since pages change often. Used prices are estimates (30–60% off the regular price) based on typical resale discounts — check the linked marketplace for real listings.

Your saved setup stays in this browser. This site has no accounts or analytics. Fonts load from Google, and store links take you to other websites.
